objects.description: Main HTTP message parser state machine object. Holds current parse state, flags, counters, version, method/status, last error, and a user data pointer. Initialize with http_parser_init(). Reused across messages as needed; consult http_should_keep_alive() and upgrade flag to manage connection lifecycle.
Callback vtable configuring how the parser reports parsed events. Zero-initialize or call http_parser_settings_init() before use, then set desired callbacks. Used with http_parser_execute().

objects.definition: typedef int (*http_data_cb) (http_parser*, const char *at, size_t length);
objects.description: Function pointer type for data callbacks (e.g., URL, status, header field/value, body). Return non-zero to signal error; may be called multiple times per field with partial data.
Function pointer type for simple event callbacks without a data buffer (e.g., message begin/complete, headers complete, chunk events). Return non-zero to signal error.
Enumeration of HTTP status codes (e.g., HTTP_STATUS_OK=200). Use with http_status_str() for human-readable strings.
Enumeration of HTTP request methods (e.g., HTTP_GET, HTTP_POST, including WebDAV/other extensions). Use with http_method_str() for names.
Parser operating mode: parse requests, responses, or both (HTTP/1.x). Supplied to http_parser_init().

objects.definition:
enum flags
  { F_CHUNKED               = 1 << 0
  , F_CONNECTION_KEEP_ALIVE = 1 << 1
  , F_CONNECTION_CLOSE      = 1 << 2
  , F_CONNECTION_UPGRADE    = 1 << 3
  , F_TRAILING              = 1 << 4
  , F_UPGRADE               = 1 << 5
  , F_SKIPBODY              = 1 << 6
  , F_CONTENTLENGTH         = 1 << 7
  };
objects.description: Bit flags used in http_parser.flags to track message properties and parser behavior (e.g., chunked, keep-alive, upgrade). Internal/semi-public; read via parser->flags.
Enumeration of parser error codes (HPE_*). Obtain current value via HTTP_PARSER_ERRNO(p). Use http_errno_name()/http_errno_description() for diagnostics.

objects.definition:
enum http_parser_url_fields
  { UF_SCHEMA           = 0
  , UF_HOST             = 1
  , UF_PORT             = 2
  , UF_PATH             = 3
  , UF_QUERY            = 4
  , UF_FRAGMENT         = 5
  , UF_USERINFO         = 6
  , UF_MAX              = 7
  };
objects.description: Enumeration of URL component indices for http_parser_url.field_data and field_set bitmask.

Result container for http_parser_parse_url(). field_set indicates which fields are present; port holds parsed numeric port; field_data provides offsets/lengths into the original buffer. Initialize with http_parser_url_init().

functions.name: http_parser_version
functions.description: Returns the library version encoded into a single unsigned long. Bits 16–23 are the major version, bits 8–15 the minor version, and bits 0–7 the patch level. Useful for feature checks and logging.
requirements: No inputs; callable at any time.
Interpret the returned value by bit-shifting as documented if you need components.

functions.name: http_parser_init
functions.description: Initializes an http_parser instance to parse either HTTP requests, responses, or both, according to type. Use before the first call to http_parser_execute, and typically before reusing a parser for a new message stream.
requirements: parser must be a valid, writable pointer.
type must be one of HTTP_REQUEST, HTTP_RESPONSE, or HTTP_BOTH.
Call before first use of parser with http_parser_execute, and before reuse for a new message stream.
The caller owns and maintains the lifetime of the parser struct storage.

functions.name: http_parser_settings_init
functions.description: Zero-initializes an http_parser_settings structure so all callbacks are set to NULL/0. Set the callbacks you need after calling this, then pass it to http_parser_execute.
requirements: settings must be a valid, writable pointer.
After initialization, set any desired callback function pointers to valid functions matching http_cb/http_data_cb signatures before use with http_parser_execute.

functions.name: http_parser_execute
functions.signature: size_t http_parser_execute(http_parser *parser, const http_parser_settings *settings, const char *data, size_t len);
functions.description: Feeds a buffer of len bytes to the HTTP parser. Drives the state machine and invokes callbacks from settings as parsing progresses. Returns the number of bytes successfully parsed; on error it sets parser->http_errno and stops (callbacks returning non-zero also stop parsing). Designed for streaming: can be called repeatedly with subsequent data chunks.
requirements: parser must be a valid pointer to a parser previously initialized with http_parser_init.
settings must be a valid pointer; its callback members may be NULL (in which case those events are ignored) or valid function pointers with the declared signatures.
data must point to a readable buffer of at least len bytes; data may be NULL only if len == 0.
Callbacks must return 0 to continue parsing; returning non-zero indicates an error and halts parsing.
In a HTTP_RESPONSE parser, on_headers_complete may return 1 to indicate no body is expected (e.g., HEAD response) or 2 to indicate no body and no further responses (e.g., CONNECT).
http_data_cb callbacks can be invoked multiple times for a single logical field; do not assume chunk boundaries map to complete strings.
When on_chunk_header is called, the current chunk length is available in parser->content_length.
After http_parser_execute returns, check both the return value and parser->http_errno; also check parser->upgrade if you need to detect Upgrade semantics.
Do not read beyond the returned parsed byte count from the input when advancing your input pointer for the next call.

functions.name: http_should_keep_alive
functions.description: Determines whether the connection should be kept alive based on the parsed message and headers (e.g., Connection and HTTP version semantics). Intended to be called in on_headers_complete or on_message_complete.
requirements: parser must be a valid pointer to a parser that has parsed at least message headers.
If this returns 0 in on_headers_complete or on_message_complete, treat the message as the last on the connection (server: send Connection: close; client: close the connection).

functions.name: http_method_str
functions.description: Returns the symbolic string name of an HTTP method (e.g., "GET", "POST") for a given enum http_method value. Useful for logging or diagnostics.
requirements: m should be a valid enum http_method value (e.g., HTTP_GET).
Behavior for invalid/unknown enum values is unspecified; callers should not pass out-of-range values.

functions.name: http_status_str
functions.description: Returns the standard reason-phrase string for an HTTP status code enum (e.g., "OK", "Not Found"). Useful for formatting responses or logs.
requirements: s should be a valid enum http_status value (e.g., HTTP_STATUS_OK).
Behavior for invalid/unknown enum values is unspecified; callers should not pass out-of-range values.

functions.name: http_errno_name
functions.description: Returns the symbolic name string (e.g., "HPE_INVALID_METHOD") corresponding to an http-parser error code. Useful for error reporting.
requirements: err should be a valid enum http_errno value, typically obtained via HTTP_PARSER_ERRNO(parser).
Behavior for invalid/unknown enum values is unspecified.

functions.name: http_errno_description
functions.description: Returns a human-readable description string for an http-parser error code (e.g., "invalid HTTP method"). Useful for diagnostics and logging.
requirements: err should be a valid enum http_errno value, typically obtained via HTTP_PARSER_ERRNO(parser).
Behavior for invalid/unknown enum values is unspecified.

functions.name: http_parser_url_init
functions.description: Zero-initializes an http_parser_url result structure. After initialization, pass it to http_parser_parse_url; then consult field_set and field_data to extract parsed components.
requirements: u must be a valid, writable pointer.
Call this before parsing a URL to clear prior contents, or ensure the struct is otherwise zero-initialized.

functions.name: http_parser_parse_url
functions.signature: int http_parser_parse_url(const char *buf, size_t buflen, int is_connect, struct http_parser_url *u);
functions.description: Parses an absolute or relative URL from buf of length buflen into the result structure u. On success, populates u->field_set bitmask and field_data offsets/lengths; converts the port (if present) to u->port. Returns nonzero on failure.
requirements: buf must point to a readable buffer of at least buflen bytes; it need not be NUL-terminated.
buflen is the exact length of the URL in bytes.
u must be a valid, writable pointer; to avoid stale data, initialize u to zero using http_parser_url_init before calling.
is_connect should be nonzero when parsing the authority form typically used with CONNECT (affects URL grammar).
After a successful parse, only index u->field_data[UF_*] when the corresponding bit is set in u->field_set; otherwise the offsets/lengths are undefined.

functions.name: http_parser_pause
functions.description: Pauses or unpauses the parser. When paused is nonzero, http_parser_execute will enter the paused state and return with HPE_PAUSED set; pass 0 to resume normal parsing on subsequent calls.
requirements: parser must be a valid pointer.
Pass a nonzero paused to pause, or 0 to unpause. The precise timing of pause effects depends on when invoked relative to http_parser_execute and callbacks.

functions.name: http_body_is_final
functions.description: Checks whether the parser is currently at the final chunk of the message body (useful for chunked transfer-encoding). Returns nonzero if the current body chunk is final.
requirements: parser must be a valid pointer.
Meaningful primarily when parsing message bodies, especially in chunked transfer scenarios.

functions.name: http_parser_set_max_header_size
functions.description: Overrides the maximum header size limit used by the parser, replacing the compile-time default (HTTP_MAX_HEADER_SIZE). Affects how much header data will be accepted before signaling overflow.
requirements: Callable at any time; applies process-wide/global to the parser implementation. Exact thread-safety and when the new limit takes effect relative to in-flight parsers are not specified in this header.
size is the new maximum in bytes; very large values effectively remove the limit.

data_types.description: Arbitrary byte buffer interpreted as an HTTP/1.x request/response stream for http_parser_execute. May contain any printable or binary bytes, including CRLF-delimited start-line, headers, optional chunked body, and can include NULs. Not required to be NUL-terminated; length is provided explicitly.

A byte buffer treated as a URL according to RFC 3986/HTTP parser rules. May be absolute or relative, may include authority, path, query, fragment, and can include NULs. Not required to be NUL-terminated; exact length is specified separately.

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generator for valid HTTP/1.x messages and fragments tailored for http_parser_execute
# Goals:
# - Produce syntactically valid start-lines (request/response)
# - Cover headers: Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding: chunked, Connection, Upgrade, Host, custom headers
# - Produce bodies consistent with headers (fixed length, chunked, none)
# - Include variations: absolute-form, origin-form, authority-form (CONNECT), asterisk-form (OPTIONS *),
#   responses with/without body (1xx, 204, 304, HEAD), chunk extensions and trailers
# - Allow partial buffers (prefixes) since the fuzzer may pass a shorter len than full buffer
# - Keep under 4096 bytes

CRLF = b"\r\n"

METHODS = [
    "GET", "POST", "PUT", "DELETE", "HEAD", "OPTIONS", "TRACE", "CONNECT", "PATCH",
    # some WebDAV/ext methods the parser recognizes
    "PROPFIND", "MKCOL", "COPY", "MOVE", "LOCK", "UNLOCK", "SEARCH", "REPORT"
]

HTTP_VERS = ["HTTP/1.0", "HTTP/1.1"]

REASONS = {
    100: "Continue", 101: "Switching Protocols", 102: "Processing",
    200: "OK", 201: "Created", 202: "Accepted", 204: "No Content",
    206: "Partial Content",
    300: "Multiple Choices", 301: "Moved Permanently", 302: "Found", 304: "Not Modified",
    307: "Temporary Redirect", 308: "Permanent Redirect",
    400: "Bad Request", 401: "Unauthorized", 403: "Forbidden", 404: "Not Found",
    405: "Method Not Allowed", 408: "Request Timeout",
    411: "Length Required", 413: "Payload Too Large", 414: "URI Too Long",
    415: "Unsupported Media Type", 418: "I'm a teapot",
    426: "Upgrade Required",
    500: "Internal Server Error", 501: "Not Implemented", 502: "Bad Gateway",
    503: "Service Unavailable", 504: "Gateway Timeout"
}

SC_NO_BODY = {100, 101, 102, 204, 304}

# Small corpus for paths, queries, hosts
PATHS = ["/", "/index.html", "/api/v1/resource", "/a/b/c", "/长路径/テスト", "/spaces here", "/%2Fencoded%20space"]
QUERIES = ["", "?q=test", "?a=1&b=2", "?empty=", "?weird=%00%FF", "?x=1; y=2"]
SCHEMES = ["http", "https"]
HOSTS = ["example.com", "localhost", "127.0.0.1", "[::1]", "xn--exmple-cua.com"]
PORTS = ["", ":80", ":443", ":8080"]

CONTENT_TYPES = [
    "text/plain; charset=utf-8",
    "application/json",
    "application/octet-stream",
    "application/x-www-form-urlencoded",
]

UPGRADES = ["websocket", "h2c", "TLS/1.0", "TLS/1.2"]

TRAILER_FIELDS = ["ETag", "Expires", "X-Trailer", "Checksum"]

# Utilities

def rand_token(r: random.Random, min_len=3, max_len=12) -> str:
    tchars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "!#$%&'*+-.^_`|~"
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(r.choice(tchars) for _ in range(n))


def rand_header_value(r: random.Random, min_len=0, max_len=20) -> str:
    # RFC allows obs-text; include some UTF-8 and spaces
    choices = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " -_/;,:.=()[]{}" + "\t"
    # sprinkle some unicode
    extra = ["µ", "✓", "§", "Ω", "Ž", "漢"]
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = "".join(r.choice(choices) for _ in range(max(0, n - 1)))
    if n > 0 and r.random() < 0.3:
        s += r.choice(extra)
    return s


def make_body(r: random.Random, min_len=0, max_len=512) -> bytes:
    # compose body with mix of text and binary
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    while sum(len(p) for p in parts) < n:
        choice = r.random()
        if choice < 0.5:
            # ascii text
            seg = ("Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. ").encode("utf-8")
        elif choice < 0.8:
            # json-like
            seg = ("{\"k\":\"v\",\"n\":" + str(r.randint(0, 1000)) + "}").encode("utf-8")
        else:
            # random bytes
            seg = bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(r.randint(8, 64)))
        parts.append(seg)
    data = b"".join(parts)[:n]
    return data


def chunk_encode(body: bytes, r: random.Random, with_trailers=True) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    i = 0
    L = len(body)
    # split into chunks of random sizes
    while i < L:
        sz = r.randint(1, min(64, L - i))
        # Optional chunk extension
        if r.random() < 0.3:
            ext = ";" + rand_token(r, 2, 6) + "=" + rand_token(r, 1, 4)
        else:
            ext = ""
        out.extend((f"{sz:x}{ext}").encode("ascii"))
        out.extend(CRLF)
        out.extend(body[i:i+sz])
        out.extend(CRLF)
        i += sz
    # final zero chunk
    out.extend(b"0")
    # maybe extension on final chunk
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        out.extend((";" + rand_token(r, 2, 6)).encode("ascii"))
    out.extend(CRLF)
    # optional trailers
    if with_trailers and r.random() < 0.7:
        ntrail = r.randint(1, 3)
        for _ in range(ntrail):
            name = r.choice(TRAILER_FIELDS)
            val = rand_header_value(r, 0, 16)
            out.extend((f"{name}: {val}").encode("utf-8"))
            out.extend(CRLF)
    # end trailers
    out.extend(CRLF)
    return bytes(out)


def build_request(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    method = r.choice(METHODS)
    version = r.choice(HTTP_VERS)

    # Choose request-target form
    form_choice = r.random()
    if method == "CONNECT" and form_choice < 0.7:
        # authority-form
        host = r.choice(HOSTS)
        port = r.choice([":443", ":80", f":{r.randint(1,65535)}"])
        target = f"{host}{port}"
    elif method == "OPTIONS" and form_choice < 0.4:
        target = "*"
    elif form_choice < 0.5:
        # absolute-form
        scheme = r.choice(SCHEMES)
        host = r.choice(HOSTS)
        port = r.choice(PORTS)
        path = r.choice(PATHS) + r.choice(QUERIES)
        target = f"{scheme}://{host}{port}{path}"
    else:
        # origin-form
        target = r.choice(PATHS) + r.choice(QUERIES)

    start_line = f"{method} {target} {version}".encode("utf-8") + CRLF

    headers: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []

    # Required Host for HTTP/1.1 (good to add often)
    if version == "HTTP/1.1" and method != "CONNECT":
        host_val = r.choice(HOSTS) + (r.choice(PORTS) if r.random() < 0.5 else "")
        headers.append(("Host", host_val))

    # Connection header variations
    conn_vals = ["keep-alive", "close"]
    if method != "CONNECT":
        conn_vals.append("upgrade")
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        headers.append(("Connection", r.choice(conn_vals)))

    # User-Agent and Accept
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        headers.append(("User-Agent", "fuzzgen/1.0"))
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        headers.append(("Accept", "*/*"))

    # Content and upgrade decisions
    send_body = method in ("POST", "PUT", "PATCH") and r.random() < 0.9
    use_chunked = send_body and r.random() < 0.5

    # Upgrade header scenario
    if r.random() < 0.2 and method in ("GET", "POST"):
        headers.append(("Upgrade", r.choice(UPGRADES)))
        if not any(h[0].lower() == "connection" for h in headers):
            headers.append(("Connection", "Upgrade"))

    if send_body:
        if r.random() < 0.6:
            headers.append(("Content-Type", r.choice(CONTENT_TYPES)))
        if use_chunked:
            headers.append(("Transfer-Encoding", "chunked"))
            body = make_body(r, 0, 256)
            payload = chunk_encode(body, r)
        else:
            body = make_body(r, 0, 256)
            headers.append(("Content-Length", str(len(body))))
            payload = body
    else:
        # no body
        payload = b""
        # sometimes explicitly set Content-Length: 0
        if r.random() < 0.4 and method in ("GET", "HEAD", "DELETE", "OPTIONS"):
            headers.append(("Content-Length", "0"))

    # Add a few random headers
    for _ in range(r.randint(0, 4)):
        headers.append((rand_token(r), rand_header_value(r)))

    # Build header section
    head = bytearray(start_line)
    for k, v in headers:
        # Optional folding via obs-fold is obsolete; avoid to keep validity
        head.extend((f"{k}: {v}").encode("utf-8"))
        head.extend(CRLF)
    head.extend(CRLF)

    return bytes(head) + payload


def build_response(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    version = r.choice(HTTP_VERS)
    status = r.choice(list(REASONS.keys()))
    reason = REASONS[status]

    start_line = f"{version} {status} {reason}".encode("utf-8") + CRLF

    headers: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []

    # Date and Server common
    if r.random() < 0.8:
        headers.append(("Server", "fuzzsrv/1.0"))
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        headers.append(("Date", "Tue, 15 Nov 1994 08:12:31 GMT"))

    # HEAD responses have no body even with Content-Length
    is_head_semantics = r.random() < 0.2

    # Decide body presence
    has_body = (status not in SC_NO_BODY) and not is_head_semantics

    # Connection header
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        headers.append(("Connection", r.choice(["keep-alive", "close"])) )

    # Upgrade scenario for 101 Switching Protocols
    if status == 101 and r.random() < 0.7:
        headers.append(("Upgrade", r.choice(UPGRADES)))
        if not any(h[0].lower() == "connection" for h in headers):
            headers.append(("Connection", "Upgrade"))

    if has_body:
        use_chunked = r.random() < 0.5 and version == "HTTP/1.1"
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            headers.append(("Content-Type", r.choice(CONTENT_TYPES)))
        if use_chunked:
            headers.append(("Transfer-Encoding", "chunked"))
            body = make_body(r, 0, 256)
            payload = chunk_encode(body, r)
        else:
            body = make_body(r, 0, 256)
            headers.append(("Content-Length", str(len(body))))
            payload = body
    else:
        payload = b""
        # Sometimes include Content-Length: 0
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            headers.append(("Content-Length", "0"))

    # Random extra headers
    for _ in range(r.randint(0, 4)):
        headers.append((rand_token(r), rand_header_value(r)))

    head = bytearray(start_line)
    for k, v in headers:
        head.extend((f"{k}: {v}").encode("utf-8"))
        head.extend(CRLF)
    head.extend(CRLF)

    return bytes(head) + payload


def maybe_multiple_messages(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a sequence of 1..3 messages back-to-back to exercise keep-alive and streaming
    msgs: List[bytes] = []
    n = r.randint(1, 3)
    for i in range(n):
        # Mix requests and responses to target HTTP_BOTH
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            msgs.append(build_request(r))
        else:
            msgs.append(build_response(r))
        # Optionally insert extraneous CRLF between messages like some servers do
        if i < n - 1 and r.random() < 0.4:
            msgs.append(CRLF)
    data = b"".join(msgs)
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a scenario profile
    profile = r.random()
    if profile < 0.25:
        buf = build_request(r)
    elif profile < 0.5:
        buf = build_response(r)
    else:
        buf = maybe_multiple_messages(r)

    # Ensure within size limit
    if len(buf) > 4096:
        buf = buf[:4096]

    return buf
